clue.text: Choice division includes the Spanish

indicators.note: includes says the division word holds the Spanish article within it

parts.note: a section is a division or part of something
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A department picks a Spanish team or staff member as its preferred option.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a pick made from several options, which is what a choice is.

clue.text: Church body upset by Welshman

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the church word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church building

explanation.surface: A church committee is annoyed by someone from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church body' looks like a governing committee, but it is the architectural body of the building, the NAVE; upset turns it to EVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typically Welsh given name, so it can stand for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Yes, cats can display delight

indicators.note: display here means the letters put on show in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Even felines can show pleasure, says someone agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges the letters of YES and CATS into the answer; 'can' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy, a strong form of delight.

clue.text: Trade vehicles on the road

explanation.surface: Commerce in cars and lorries driving along.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means dealing or commerce (often illicit) and also the flow of cars and lorries on a street.

clue.text: Food served in Salerno at six

indicators.note: served in says the food is tucked away inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A meal dished up in an Italian town at six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain eaten as porridge, so they are a foodstuff.

clue.text: Intensive discussion, mind, must precede assault

indicators.note: must precede says the mind word comes before the assault word in the answer

parts.note: the brain is the mind or intellect
storming is attacking a position by force

explanation.surface: A heated debate where the intellect leads the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainstorming is a group session of rapid idea-sharing, a concentrated kind of talk.

clue.text: Gipsies delight to see a climber

parts.note: travellers is a name used in Britain for gipsies and other itinerant people
joy is delight or great pleasure

explanation.surface: Wandering people are thrilled to spot a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant: traveller's joy is wild clematis, common in British hedgerows.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is the wild clematis, a plant that clambers over hedges, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Brothers light on will-o'-the-wisp

parts.note: friars are members of religious orders, addressed as Brother
a lantern is a portable light

explanation.surface: Monks shine a lamp on a flickering marsh glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar's lantern is an old folk name for the ghostly marsh light also called ignis fatuus.

clue.text: Players I confine and reprimand

parts.note: the cast are the players in a play
to gate a pupil is to confine them to school grounds as a punishment, a British school usage

explanation.surface: An actor says they keep the company in and tell it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, a strong form of telling off.

clue.text: Eccentric man adored by a cluster of stars

indicators.note: eccentric signals the letters of the following words behave oddly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd fellow is worshipped by a group of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities, but the definition is astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a named grouping of stars, also home to a nearby galaxy.

clue.text: Opposed to laying a snare

parts.note: a gin is a trap or snare for catching game

explanation.surface: Someone is against setting a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form meaning against, so it means being set against something.

clue.text: Faux pas made by boss endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the boss word loses its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: An embarrassing slip committed by the person in charge, without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, which is what the French faux pas means.

clue.text: Part of stove normally used for roasts

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a cooker is ordinarily where joints are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the heated chamber in which meat joints are cooked.

clue.text: Simpleton finds lodging in new York

indicators.note: in says the lodging word sits inside the letters for the city

parts.note: an inn offers lodging to travellers

explanation.surface: A foolish person gets a room in the big American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a silly or foolish person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Cute girl in Cyprus

indicators.note: in says the girl's name goes inside the country's code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cute' reads as pretty, but here it is the older sense, shrewd or clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd, and cute in its older sense is likewise sharp-witted.

clue.text: Examine whether unknown character should bear witness

parts.note: to test is to examine
if can mean whether, as in 'ask if'
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Investigate whether a mysterious person ought to give evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence under oath, as a witness does.

clue.text: Slow walker who is quick to ingratiate himself

definitions.text: who is quick to ingratiate himself

explanation.surface: A slowcoach who is nonetheless fast at currying favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler moves slowly on all fours, and is also a toady who fawns to win favour.

clue.text: Reasons for having a lot of land

explanation.surface: Why someone might own an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are the justifications for an action, and also the land surrounding a large house.

clue.text: Such footwear makes him lose his footing

definitions.text: Such footwear makes him lose his footing

parts.words: Such footwear makes him lose his footing
parts.note: a soft indoor shoe that is named as if it were a person who stumbles and slides

explanation.surface: This kind of shoe makes a man fall over.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a loose house shoe, and the word also names one who slides and falls.

clue.text: Ray of light makes retired seamen smile

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the seamen's initials are read backwards

parts.note: NUS was the National Union of Seamen, a British trade union
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A sunny glint makes old sailors grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired seamen' suggests old sailors; it is the National Union of Seamen, NUS, reversed to SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a shaft of sunlight, a single ray.

clue.text: Pole wearing a hood looked menacing

parts.note: S is short for the South Pole
cowled means wearing a cowl, a monk's hood

explanation.surface: A Polish man in a hood appeared threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person, but it is a compass pole giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown angrily, so scowled means glowered threateningly.

clue.text: Back issue of us news magazine

indicators.note: back says the issue word is read from right to left

parts.note: to issue is to emit or send out

explanation.surface: An old edition of an American current-affairs weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is a long-running American weekly news periodical.

clue.text: Navigator I left in a vessel

indicators.note: in says the letters for I and left go inside the vessel

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: A sailor says they set off in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container, a POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers a ship into harbour or flies an aircraft, guiding its course.

clue.text: Employed, but exploited

explanation.surface: Someone was given a job but taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means put to work or applied, and also taken unfair advantage of.

clue.text: Steering apparatus made of hardwood

parts.note: H stands for hard, as on pencil grades
elm is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A ship's wheel is built from tough timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardwood' looks like one word, but it splits into hard (H) and wood (ELM).
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel by which a vessel is steered.

clue.text: School English heavyweight

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: A large English schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is a famous English public (private boarding) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English boarding establishment for boys.

clue.text: Police worldwide at one about spurious entry

parts.note: Interpol is the international criminal police organisation
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: International police, all together, look into a false record.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpolation is text inserted into a document that was not in the original, a bogus addition.

clue.text: Unwise but bold enough to imprison ringleader

indicators.note: to imprison says the bold word encloses the ringleader's letter

parts.note: impudent means cheeky or bold
the leader of ring, its first letter, is R

explanation.surface: Foolish but brazen enough to lock up the gang's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means rash, lacking good sense or caution.
